name: Radboud University
summary: Campus university in Nijmegen with 14 English-taught bachelor's, from AI and Molecular Life Sciences to Psychology and American Studies.

ib.text: The IB Diploma is assessed individually against the Dutch VWO. English A SL/HL at 4+ or English B HL at 6+ covers English. Strictest maths: Maths AA HL (Computing Science, AI).

programmes.name: American Studies
programmes.about: The United States studied through its politics, society, history, literature, media and language, in full English immersion, with the option of a semester in the US or an internship. A specialisation of English Language and Culture.
programmes.overview: You study American society, politics, history, culture and language, including American literature, media and the arts, political institutions and the role of the United States in global affairs. Teaching is fully in English, with a strong focus on building written and spoken English at a professional level and on communication skills. Study abroad in the United States and internships are possible. The degree is a specialisation within the Bachelor of Arts in English Language and Culture at the Faculty of Arts in Nijmegen. Graduates work in international relations, education, journalism and other fields that value analytical and communication skills.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL at 4+, at least 24 points and three HL subjects (2025/26 criteria; 2027 not yet published).
programmes.about: AI with a special focus on understanding and simulating the brain, taught alongside the Donders Institute and the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics on campus; programming is taught from scratch.
programmes.overview: The programme combines mathematics and computing science with psychology and neuroscience, logic and linguistics, with a special place for understanding and simulating the brain. Programming is taught from the basics at a pace suited to beginners, first-year students get mentoring support, and electives let you shape your own programme or spend part of it studying abroad. The programme works closely with several research institutes. Graduates work in education, research, healthcare, telecommunications, ICT, transport and financial services, and many are hired before they graduate.

needs.note: If short, a maths test (SAT Maths 600+, OMPT 55%) can make up the gap.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. 2025/26 IB criteria (Maths AA HL 4, 24 points, 3 HL); 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Arts and Culture Studies
programmes.about: Visual arts, literature, (pop) music, film, television and theatre studied side by side in small international classes, learning to write sharp reviews and to curate art with its audience in mind.
programmes.overview: You study cultural expressions across visual arts, literature, pop and classical music, film, television and theatre, using theoretical, historical, political and social perspectives. Questions include what counts as art, how popular culture relates to society, and how Western and non-Western views differ. Classes are small, interactive and international, and the degree leaves room for a minor and free electives. Graduates work as programme curators for theatres or festivals, reviewers of books or films, or government policy officers, in cultural organisations, government, publishing, research institutes or education.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Biology
programmes.ib: Biology HL, Chemistry HL; Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL; physics before the DP; 27 points excl. core, every grade 4+. Group 6 arts don't count: take a 2nd science.
programmes.about: A broad biology degree across seven domains, from molecules to ecosystems, with heavy lab and field time (30+ contact hours in year 1) and internships at Radboud's research institutes.
programmes.overview: The programme covers seven domains of biology, from evolution, brain function and plant genetics to ecology, the effects of climate change on biodiversity, disease diagnosis and the chemistry of DNA and RNA. Teaching is interactive and team-based, with laboratory work in modern research facilities and internships at three research institutes (RIBES, RIMLS and DCN). After the foundation year you specialise and design your own profile, choosing courses from both biology and medical biology. Graduates work as researchers, teachers, consultants, policymakers or managers in profit and non-profit organisations.

needs.note: Physics taken before the DP (MYP or IGCSE) is enough.

programmes.selectionNote: No longer numerus fixus: everyone who meets the 2027-28 requirements and applies on time gets a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery.

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.ib: Physics, Chemistry and Maths AA (not AI), two at HL; 27 points excl. core, every grade 4+. Group 6 arts don't count: replace with a second science.
programmes.about: Chemistry with a solid theoretical base and extensive lab training, working on new medicines and sustainable materials with high-tech research facilities such as the high-field magnet lab.
programmes.overview: You study organic, physical and biochemistry alongside the mathematical and physical concepts behind molecular processes. Lectures are combined with thorough practical training: through experiments you study chemical reactions and use specialised techniques that rely on lasers and magnetic fields to study materials. With more than 25 chemistry research groups working on sustainability, drug development, data storage and the origin of life, you can choose the direction in which to specialise. Graduates work in industrial or university research, in education with a teaching qualification, or in consulting and management, or continue to related master programmes such as Molecular Life Sciences.

needs.note: AI is not accepted. Two of Maths AA, Physics and Chemistry must be HL.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Computing Science
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL (AA SL and AI are not accepted); 27 points (excluding core), every grade 4+.
programmes.about: Programming built on its mathematical foundations, with strong cyber security and AI groups; you build software for real clients in the student company GiPHouse and try new devices in the lab.
programmes.overview: You learn programming, how software works, how data is represented digitally, the mathematical and logical principles behind computing, how hardware is built into computers and networks, and how to protect IT systems through cybersecurity. Practical work includes GiPHouse, a student software company that works for real customers, and the New Devices Lab for experimenting with new gadgets, as well as courses on processor assembly language. Cyber security and AI are particular strengths of the Nijmegen programme. Graduates take IT roles across many sectors, and most find work before they graduate; the university AI master is a related option.

needs.note: AA SL and AI are not accepted.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Economics
programmes.ib: Maths must be in your diploma at a sufficient level, checked individually; if not, pass a maths test (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).
programmes.about: Economics seen through accounting, finance and international economics and policy; after the first year you choose one of these as your specialisation. Same content as the Dutch-taught version.
programmes.overview: The first year introduces the foundations of economics and three areas in which you can later specialise: accounting, finance, and international economics and policy. You develop an analytical perspective and learn research methods that connect theory to real-world questions. After year one you choose one of the three specialisation tracks. Most students continue to a master, and others work in consulting, banking, insurance or government organisations, in roles that call for rigorous economic analysis and prediction.

needs.note: Level checked individually; if short, pass a maths test (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: English Language and Culture
programmes.about: A research-based degree joining English linguistics, literature, culture, society and history, with language-acquisition courses from day one and the option to study abroad or intern.
programmes.overview: You study the English language and linguistics, literature from English-speaking regions, including classics of high and popular culture, and the culture, history, social relations and customs of Great Britain and other English-speaking communities. Teaching is fully in English, with a strong focus on language development and communication skills, and the degree includes study abroad and hands-on internship experience. You follow either the English Language and Culture pathway or the American Studies pathway. Graduates work in communication, education, and culture and heritage.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: International Business Administration
programmes.ib: Maths must be in your diploma at a sufficient level, checked individually; if not, pass a maths test (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).
programmes.about: Marketing, HRM, strategy and other business processes studied as one system in an international context, with a focus on responsible and sustainable organisations and a flexible third-year semester.
programmes.overview: You study international management together with psychology and sociology, communication and economics, law, marketing, human resources management and strategy, with a focus on responsible and sustainable organisations and entrepreneurship. The aim is to understand how organisations create social and economic value, and you build research skills for critically assessing scientific knowledge. A flexible semester in year three lets you follow your own interests, with optional study abroad and international internships.

needs.note: Level checked individually; if short, pass a maths test (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: International Business Communication
programmes.ib: Maths must be one of your final-exam subjects; otherwise a maths certificate (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).

separateFrom.name: International Business Administration
separateFrom.reason: A different degree (BA, not BSc) in business communication, with its own maths rule: maths as a final-exam subject or a maths certificate.

programmes.about: How organisations communicate across languages and cultures: intercultural and professional communication, scenario-based projects, and academic English or Spanish. The English-taught track of Communication and Information Studies.
programmes.overview: You study language and communication theory applied to business, with intercultural communication, professional English and an optional Spanish specialisation, and learn to analyse language and communication processes scientifically. Classes are small and interactive, and scenario-based projects, such as designing an advertising campaign or developing a marketing plan, apply the theory directly while building consultancy, report-writing and research skills. Study abroad, a minor and free electives are possible. Graduates work in multinational companies, government organisations, NGOs, consultancy firms and educational institutions.

needs.note: Maths must be a final-exam subject; otherwise a maths certificate (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Molecular Life Sciences
programmes.ib: Physics, Chemistry and Maths AA (not AI), two at HL; 27 points excl. core, every grade 4+. Group 6 arts don't count: replace with a second science.
programmes.about: Chemistry, biology and medical science combined to work on molecular solutions to medical problems, with lectures, computer practicals and hands-on lab experiments from the start.
programmes.overview: The first year builds on physics and mathematics, chemistry and biology, and looks at molecular processes from a biomedical angle: how cells work in health and disease and how multicellular organisms function. You learn through lectures, seminars and hands-on lab experiments in high-tech research facilities. Ten years after graduating, those without a PhD tend to hold managerial roles in technological settings, while PhD holders move into specialist positions with management responsibility or research roles at universities in the Netherlands and abroad.

needs.note: AI is not accepted. Two of Maths AA, Physics and Chemistry must be HL.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Natural Sciences
programmes.ib: Physics, Chemistry and Maths AA (not AI), two at HL; 27 points excl. core, every grade 4+. Group 6 arts don't count: replace with a second science.
programmes.about: Physics, chemistry and biology integrated into one programme with mathematics, with access to facilities such as the FELIX laser lab and the High Field Magnet Laboratory.
programmes.overview: Physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics are taught at their intersection in a broad but rigorous first year, with extensive guidance from accessible teaching staff and laboratory work. Later you specialise in one of three directions: physical-chemical, biological-physical or biological-chemical, with advanced topics such as quantum mechanics, nanoscience, biophysics, DNA techniques and the analysis of molecular biological data. Graduates work in industry on scientific innovations such as solar cells, microchips and biodegradable plastics, in research needing interdisciplinary approaches, or as teachers, who are in high demand.

needs.note: AI is not accepted. Two of Maths AA, Physics and Chemistry must be HL.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Philosophy, Politics and Society
programmes.about: An issue-led philosophy degree: the curriculum is built around themes such as ecological crisis, the future of technology, identity politics and the global political order, and the ideas behind them.
programmes.overview: The first year introduces Western philosophy through four courses on its history, plus systematic courses in political philosophy, ethics, metaphysics and philosophical anthropology and the philosophy of science, alongside four courses in academic skills and methods. Classes are interactive, and in years two and three you follow modules of three courses on themes such as global justice, human rights, digital technology and ecological challenges, finishing with a bachelor thesis. Most students continue to a specialised master, and graduates work in policy analysis, think tanks, journalism, government, consultancy and NGOs.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you get a place. Apply early in Studielink to join the housing lottery; a non-binding compatibility check follows.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (600 places): apply by 15 January; ranked on a matching assignment (60%) and grades (40%). Maths AI at 4+ or AA at 3+.
programmes.about: A broad psychology degree tied to research in brain and cognition, development and mental health, and behaviour and environment, with electives from year 2 and an optional semester abroad in year 3.
programmes.overview: You study human behaviour, mind and emotion: how the brain controls behaviour, how people develop from infancy to old age, and how environment and social context shape thinking, action and feeling. Research areas are Brain & Cognition, Development & Mental Health, and Behaviour & Environment, and practical research is part of the training. From year two you choose more of your own courses, and in year three you can study abroad, for example in Australia, Japan or South Africa. Graduates work in aid, education, human resources, public policy, counselling, training, coaching, sport and advertising.

needs.note: Maths AA at grade 3 is also accepted; otherwise a maths test (e.g. SAT Maths 600+).

programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January. Ranked on a matching assignment due 15 February (60%) and your grades (40%); ranking numbers come on 15 April.

notes: Binding study advice: you must earn 39 to 45 of the 60 first-year credits, depending on the faculty (39 in Science, 45 in Arts), or leave the programme.
Economics and Psychology also run Dutch-taught or bilingual versions, so pick the English-taught one in Studielink.
Non-selective programmes include a Study Compatibility Check (an online questionnaire, sometimes an interview) whose advice is not binding.
